sections.history: Tirukkollampudur, whose historical name is Kollamputhur, lies about 22–24 km from Kumbakonam near Koradacheri and Nidamangalam, in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar, and is counted among the Pancha Aranya Kshetrams, the five forest shrines of the Kumbakonam country, as the vilva (bael) forest. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later. The same village holds the Pereyil Jagadeeswarar temple, another Paadal Petra Sthalam.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Vilvaranyeswarar — 'lord of the vilva forest' — in the sanctum, with the goddess Soundara Nayaki in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the vilva (bael), the leaf dearest to Shiva, which gives the shrine its forest name. The Vettaru river flows nearby.
sections.legends: The great story of the place belongs to the child-saint Sambandar, who came to worship here but found the Vettaru river in heavy flood, barring his way. By the power of his devotion and song — in some tellings taking a boat across, in others the waters themselves yielding — he reached the shrine and sang the lord's praise. As a vilva-forest shrine of the Pancha Aranya set, the temple is loved by those who make the round of the five forests, and the vilva leaf is central to its worship.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims making the round of the Pancha Aranya forests and the Paadal Petra temples include Tirukkollampudur among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tirukkollampudur the pilgrim comes to a bael-forest shrine of the Pancha Aranya, rich in the memory of Sambandar crossing the Vettaru. Before Vilvaranyeswarar, lord of the vilva, and the beautiful Soundara Nayaki, the visitor offers the sacred bael leaf in a quiet Tevaram temple of the Kaveri country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirukkollampudur is about 22–24 km from Kumbakonam, near Koradacheri and Nidamangalam (Chellur, via Kudavasal), in Tiruvarur district. Kumbakonam and Nidamangalam are the nearest rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
